title: Takara
text:
'''Takara''' was a Japanese toy company that published Japanese-language [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]] products in partnership with [[Decipher]].<ref name="encyclopedia">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 41–45. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Company history ==
Takara's predecessor, Sato Vinyl Industry, was established in 1955. In 2006, Takara merged with Tomy to form Takara Tomy.<ref name="history">[https://www.takaratomy.co.jp/company/history.html Company history], Takara Tomy. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20150424004951/http://www.takaratomy.co.jp:80/company/history.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="merger">[https://www.takaratomy.co.jp/english/ir/etc/faq.html Investor relations FAQ], Takara Tomy. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20111120003649/http://www.takaratomy.co.jp:80/english/ir/etc/faq.html Internet Archive].</ref>

== Star Wars CCG ==
Takara's Japanese products included [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere]] in 1997, [[A New Hope (Japanese)|A New Hope]] in 1997, and [[Hoth (Japanese)|Hoth]] in 1998. It also published the Japanese [[Premiere Introductory Two-Player Game (Japanese)|Premiere]] and [[The Empire Strikes Back Introductory Two-Player Game (Japanese)|Empire Strikes Back]] introductory two-player games.<ref name="encyclopedia" />

Japanese Premiere was sold in 15-card booster packs and 60-card starter sets; the starter set included a Japanese rulebook. Takara also issued Japanese player’s guides. The Japanese introductory two-player products contained two preconstructed 60-card decks, a booster pack, and Japanese rules materials. The Empire Strikes Back product also included a sample-game booklet.<ref name="encyclopedia" />
